glyph_origin: Pictogram (象形): a standing person facing forward. Compare 人, which represents the profile of a person. Often explained as an ideogram of a person with outstretched arms; however, the ancient scripts do not show stretching. Compare with 尢, which is a man with bent legs. Compare also 立, similar to 大, and 交, in which the legs are crossed. Compare also 文, which is a man with arms outstretched and a crest or tattoo on his chest, and to 夭, which is a man with arms outstretched and leaning to side (running or marching vigorously). See the top component of 泰 in the original version (𡙌), the top component of 赤 and the bottom component of 奐 (well visible in some fonts). Related to 太. Unrelated to 买, in which the bottom component is the stylization of a cowrie.
senses: [dà] of great size; big; large; huge
